issue.body:
### What happened?

As the HIP runtime driver is built and deployed with IREE pip packages, and is generally slated to be the canonical HAL driver for rocm devices, I have noticed (alongside the known performance caveats) a numerics issue that is isolated to the HAL driver execution on my 7900xtx (gfx1100 chip)

The same .vmfbs compiled for gfx1100 produce good results on config B unet (config A blocked by lowering issues, see: https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/17032) using the _rocm_ driver, but using _hip_ driver yields NaNs.

We don't want to be using config B (attention decomposed into bmm->softmax->bmm at torch fx graph level), but I believe this is still indicative of a genuine bug in the hip HAL driver.

I will update this issue as soon as I have some specific dispatch to point to -- breaking at flow dispatches to check output validity is difficult with the async-external execution model, as the CLI has issues with parsing the async dispatch symbols and specifying them verbatim from the flow IR or dispatch graph doesn't always work, so I will continue on this with tensor trace ops.

### Steps to reproduce your issue

_No response_

### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

Runtime

### Version information

IREE (https://iree.dev):
  openxla/iree@5d8907e82f
  LLVM version 19.0.0git
  Optimized build with assertions

### Additional context

_No response_

This patch retires the ROCm HAL backend given the new HIP HAL backend is functionally complete (https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/15790). The new backend has been tested and proved to give on par or better performance compared to the ROCm backend.

The documentation still preserves the `ROCm` term to denote the AMD compute software while using `HIP` specifically for the runtime.

### What happened?

The same .vmfb gives different results on ROCM and HIP hal drivers. Caching allocator is being used on both, but this doesn't seem to make a difference if disabled.

Good numerics: ROCM with inlined weights gives correct output.

Bad numerics # 1: ROCM with external weights gives all zeroes output

Bad numerics # 2: HIP with inlined weights gives wrong numbers.

Bad numerics # 3: HIP with external weights gives wrong numbers.

I am filing this issue specifically for this target and IR because other targets and models do not reproduce the same success/failure cases. (see https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/17033)


The only reason I am including ROCM HAL results is because they contain the only success mode. We should focus on fixing HIP hal issues.

Wow big news, actually, as I was about to give the IREE cli version of this:

quite shocking. the issue must lie outside of IREE hal driver in this case. I will check if the same applies to SDXL unet.

So I tracked down at least one issue (in unet). If you run `iree-run-module .... --parameter_mode=preload`  that seems to largely fix the issues I am seeing. Still digging into / fixing the underlying issue.
This looks to be an issue in the windows hip driver. A fix is being made there.
Thanks both @monorimet and @AWoloszyn for the great investigation. We know the issue now and also have a shorterm workaround. I'll close this one.
